Zsurk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zsurk, Hungary

Not demolished. Zsurk's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map and was later enlarged, with its newer section fenced separately; its oldest surviving tombstone dates to 1891, its newest to 1936. Jews first settled in the village in the late 18th century, growing from 20 residents in 1840 to a peak of 98 by 1910, before declining to 71 by 1941. The community joined the Orthodox stream following the 1869 Schism in Hungarian Jewry. According to Yad Vashem records, about 55 of Zsurk's Jews were murdered in the Holocaust.
